about.title: National City Medical Malpractice Claims
about.longDescription: National City residents rely on a mix of local clinics, urgent care centers, and San Diego County hospital systems for everything from routine visits to emergency treatment. Most of the time, care goes as expected. But when a provider misses a diagnosis, makes a surgical error, or mishandles medication, the effects can follow a patient for years. California law recognizes that not every bad outcome is malpractice — a claim requires showing the provider fell below the accepted standard of care and that this failure caused real harm. These cases are technical, often requiring a qualified medical expert to review records and testify, and they move on a strict legal clock. Our team handles medical malpractice claims directly and can evaluate what happened, explain your options in plain language, and help you understand whether pursuing a claim makes sense for your situation.

whyChoose.title: Why National City Residents Choose Us

items.title: MICRA's Deadlines Are Unforgiving
items.desc: California generally gives you one year from discovering the injury, and no more than three years from the date it occurred, plus a required 90-day pre-suit notice — we can help you track these dates before they pass.

items.title: Expert Review Is Almost Always Required
items.desc: Because malpractice cases hinge on proving a provider deviated from accepted medical standards, a qualified medical expert typically has to weigh in — our team can help arrange that kind of review.

items.title: Damages Caps Change Over Time
items.desc: California's cap on non-economic damages rises each year under current law, so understanding how it applies to your timeline matters, and we can walk you through what that means for your specific claim.

items.question: How long do I have to file a medical malpractice claim in National City?
items.answer: Under California's MICRA rules, you generally have one year from when you discovered (or reasonably should have discovered) the injury, but never more than three years from the date it happened. There's also a required 90-day notice before filing suit against the provider. Because these deadlines can be confusing, it's worth having an attorney review your specific dates as soon as possible.

items.question: Is a bad medical outcome automatically malpractice?
items.answer: No — California law requires proof that a provider's care fell below the accepted medical standard and that this failure directly caused harm. A poor result alone, even a serious one, doesn't automatically mean malpractice occurred. We can help assess whether your situation meets that legal bar, often working with a medical expert.

items.question: Which National City facilities are involved in malpractice claims you see?
items.answer: We handle claims involving any hospital, clinic, or urgent care facility that serves the National City area, including those along corridors like National City Boulevard or E Plaza Boulevard. What matters most is the specific care you received and whether it met the required standard, which we can evaluate case by case.

items.question: Do you charge anything for a case review?
items.answer: No, our initial case review is completely free. If we take your case, we typically work on contingency, meaning there's no fee unless you recover compensation.
